title: Wave Is All You Need: A Quantum Language Model Based on Fully Connected Quantum Boltzmann Machine
abstract: This work proposes a self-attention mechanism based on the fully connected quantum Boltzmann machine (FC-QBM), and further constructs a fully connected quantum Boltzmann machine language model (FC-QBM-LM) using the mechanism as the core engine. By performing unitary evolution on semantic quantum states, the mechanism implicitly implements positional encoding and self-attention computation, eliminating the need to decompose continuous semantic streams into discrete matrices for explicit matrix multiplication, with the measurement results naturally satisfying the normalization condition. Specifically, this work rigorously derives the computational principle of the self-attention mechanism based on FC-QBM, and demonstrates that this mechanism is mathematically equivalent to the classical self-attention mechanism. The mathematical principles governing the training and generation of FC-QBM-LM are thoroughly derived, and the two corresponding algorithms are subsequently developed. An 8-qubit FC-QBM-LM is finally constructed and trained on the corpus of Tang poetry. Under the 8-qubit setting, the quantum layer implements the entire positional encoding and self-attention computation pipeline with only 44 parameters. In the noiseless scenario, the model exhibits favorable convergence. Furthermore, the quantum circuit proposed in this work, which terminates with Y-axis rotation gates, achieves better convergence than the counterpart terminating with X-axis rotation gates. Under the small-sample regime and across eight distinct noise intensity levels, the model demonstrates strong noise robustness, retaining over 99% of its noiseless convergence performance. Experiments on five-character quatrain generation reveal that the model preliminarily exhibits three core capabilities: associative and divergent thinking, content generation across imagery and human-aligned word ordering.
summary: This work introduces an FC-QBM-LM to replace classical self-attention in language models, aiming to preserve continuous semantic information while reducing computational overhead. By implementing attention via unitary quantum evolution, the model achieves strong noise robustness and demonstrates preliminary generative capabilities on poetry. It represents a novel quantum approach to core NLP components.
main_problem: The paper addresses the limitations of classical self-attention mechanisms in Language Models (LLMs), specifically the loss of continuous semantic information and high computational complexity.
main_result: The proposed FC-QBM-LM demonstrates strong noise robustness, retaining over 99% of its noiseless performance, and preliminarily shows capabilities like associative and divergent thinking in poetry generation.
method: It proposes using a Fully Connected Quantum Boltzmann Machine (FC-QBM) to implicitly implement self-attention and positional encoding via unitary quantum evolution, mathematically proving its equivalence to classical attention.
model_or_system: The model is an 8-qubit FC-QBM-LM trained on Tang poetry, where the quantum layer handles the entire self-attention and positional encoding pipeline using only 44 parameters.
key_observables: Convergence performance (MSE), Noise Robustness (Retention Rate), and generative quality (associative/divergent thinking in quatrain generation).
important_parameters: 8 qubits, 44 parameters, noise intensities up to 8x baseline noise.
main_assumptions: The quantum mechanism is mathematically equivalent to the classical self-attention mechanism, and the results might be specific to the small-sample regime.
figures_summary: Figure 6 shows generated five-character quatrains from different training epochs, illustrating the model's evolving coherence and imagery.
paper_structure: The paper reviews classical self-attention limitations, proposes the FC-QBM-LM as a quantum replacement, derives the mathematical principles, constructs and trains the model on Tang poetry, and evaluates its performance under noise and on generation tasks.
why_interesting: It applies quantum machine learning techniques (QBMs) to a complex, high-dimensional data structure (language), offering a quantum perspective on overcoming computational bottlenecks inherent in modern AI architectures.
